facts.text: Earlier fundamental rights studied were the rights of liberty, equality and the right against exploitation.
facts.quote: We studied the rights of liberty, equality and the right against exploitation.

facts.text: India is an important secular country in the world.
facts.quote: India, we know, is an important secular country in the world.

facts.text: Under the right to freedom of religion, each Indian citizen is free to practise any religion and to establish institutions for religious reasons.
facts.quote: According to it, each Indian citizen is free to practise any religion and to establish institutions for religious reasons.

facts.text: In order to broaden the scope of the right to freedom of religion, two things are not permitted.
facts.quote: In order to broaden the scope of the right to freedom of religion, two things are not permitted

facts.text: The State cannot impose religious taxes that might be used to encourage a particular religion; the Constitution forbids religious taxes.
facts.quote: State cannot impose religious taxes that might be used to encourage a particular religion. That is, our Constitution forbids religious taxes.

facts.text: Religious education cannot be made compulsory in educational institutions that receive aid from the State.
facts.quote: Religious education cannot be made compulsory in educational institutions that receive aid from the State.

facts.text: India has a great diversity of festivals, food and ways of life; these, like different wedding ceremonies, are part of the cultures of different communities.
facts.quote: there is a great diversity of festivals, food and ways of life in our country ... All these things are part of the cultures of the different communities.

facts.text: Under Cultural and Educational Rights, the Constitution has given different communities the right to preserve their cultural uniqueness.
facts.quote: Our Constitution has given the different communities the right to preserve their cultural uniqueness.

facts.text: People are free to preserve their own language, script and literature and also to make efforts towards their promotion.
facts.quote: people are not only free to preserve their own language, script and literature, but also make efforts towards their promotion.

facts.text: People can establish institutions for the development of their language.
facts.quote: They can establish institutions for the development of their language.

facts.text: The citizens' right to get judicial remedies when fundamental rights are encroached upon is itself a fundamental right, called the Right to Constitutional Remedies.
facts.quote: In case of encroachment of fundamental rights, the Indian citizens' right to get judicial remedies is also a fundamental right. This is called the Right to Constitutional Remedies.

facts.text: The Constitution itself has provided for legal remedies in case people's rights get violated.
facts.quote: This means the Constitution itself has provided for legal remedies in case people's rights get violated.

facts.text: It is a constitutional duty of the courts to protect the rights of the people.
facts.quote: So, it becomes a constitutional duty of the courts to protect the rights of the people.

facts.text: When our constitutional rights are encroached upon and we are not able to exercise them, it is called an infringement of our rights.
facts.quote: Sometimes the rights that are guaranteed to us by the Constitution may get encroached upon and we are not able to exercise our rights. This is called an infringement of our rights.

facts.text: The court considers the complaint, investigates it and, if convinced that rights were infringed and injustice done, gives an appropriate verdict.
facts.quote: The court considers our complaint, investigates it and in case it is convinced that rights have indeed been infringed upon and injustice has been done to the aggrieved individual, the court gives an appropriate verdict.

facts.text: Arresting an individual without reason is an instance of infringement of rights.
facts.quote: Some instances of infringement of rights: Arresting an individual without reason.

facts.text: Preventing a person from leaving a village or a town without giving a valid reason is an instance of infringement of rights.
facts.quote: Preventing a person from leaving a village or a town without giving a valid reason.

facts.text: Refusing food, water or medicines to jail inmates is an instance of infringement of rights.
facts.quote: Refusing food, water or medicines to jail inmates.

facts.text: Courts have powers to issue various kinds of writs to protect the rights of the citizens; five writs are listed.
facts.quote: Courts have powers to issue various kinds of writs to protect the rights of the citizens.

facts.text: Habeas Corpus: protection from unlawful arrest and detention.
facts.quote: (1) Habeas Corpus : Protection from unlawful arrest and detention.

facts.text: Mandamus: the order of the Courts (the Supreme Court or the High Court) commanding the government to perform an action that is its duty to perform in public interest.
facts.quote: (2) Mandamus : The order of the Courts (the Supreme Court or the High Court) commanding the government to perform an action that is its duty to perform in public interest.

facts.text: Prohibition: to prevent a subordinate court from exceeding its jurisdiction.
facts.quote: (3) Prohibition : To prevent a subordinate court from exceeding its jurisdiction.

facts.text: Quo Warranto: to restrain a person from acting in an office to which he is not entitled.
facts.quote: (4) Quo Warranto : To restrain a person from acting in an office to which he is not entitled.

facts.text: Certiorari: to order the removal of a law suit from a subordinate court to a superior court.
facts.quote: (5) Certiorari : To order the removal of a law suit from a subordinate court to a superior court.

facts.text: An officer told a woman who presented all the documents for a scheme for destitutes, "You don't look like a destitute", and refused her the benefits.
facts.quote: An officer tells a woman who presents all the documents for getting the benefits of a scheme for destitutes, "You don't look like a destitute" and refuses her the benefits of the scheme.

facts.text: Because the fundamental rights are protected by the courts, citizens are able to exercise their rights and fulfil their roles as alert, responsible and active citizens.
facts.quote: Because the fundamental rights are thus protected by the courts, citizens are able to exercise their rights. They can fulfil their roles as alert, responsible and active citizens.

facts.text: While considering fundamental rights, we also need to remember our duties.
facts.quote: While considering fundamental rights, we also need to remember our duties.
